Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood inference — procurement & commercial path

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with procurement requirements.

What we covered:
- Demo of hosted API (low-friction) and dedicated/reserved options for PII workloads
- Key SLOs we discussed: p50 latency targets, expected throughput for 50 concurrent sessions
- High level pricing: on-demand hosting vs 1yr commit (savings with commits) vs dedicated reserved pools

Procurement questions to confirm:
1) Billing preference: PO / invoice (Net30) vs card?
2) Marketplace interest (AWS Marketplace) to route billing through their procurement system?
3) If we need Private (VPC/on-prem) for PII workloads or dedicated reserved capacity is sufficient?
4) Any internal contracting requirements (PO number, SOC2 evidence, SCCs)?

Next steps:
- I will share a short commercial note outlining packaging options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), commit bands and typical billing flows (card, PO, marketplace) — ETA: tomorrow.
- If procurement prefers PO/Net terms or marketplace routing, I’ll loop in Aditya (sales ops) and Soojin (sales & legal ops) to coordinate paperwork and next steps.
- Please send over any procurement questionnaire or standard contract redlines when convenient.

Attachments: demo-deck.pdf (slide highlights referenced in call)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood inference — procurement & commercial path

Thanks Marissa, good session — a few answers from procurement side: 

- Billing: We require a PO and invoice processing. Our default is Net30, finance will prefer PO rather than card for anything > $10k/month.
- Marketplace: Yes — if you can be listed on AWS Marketplace and support consolidated billing, that speeds procurement and our security review.
- Deployment: For general user-facing product we prefer hosted. For PII-sensitive models certain teams will require either Dedicated reserved pools or Private (VPC) depending on data residency.
- Commit: We're most likely to look at a 1yr commit for the first phase to get predictable costs; range TBD based on your pricing bands.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire they asked us to fill in (we still need to confirm one section). I've CC'd procurement@acmecorp.com so they can chime in on contract language and invoicing cadence.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick clarifications and for looping in procurement. See inline summary and recommended commercial path below.

(Quoted)
> - Billing: We require a PO and invoice processing. Our default is Net30, finance will prefer PO rather than card for anything > $10k/month.

Recommended approach:
- Billing flow: For PO/Net30 we’ll route through our enterprise billing (invoices). Aditya (cc’d) will own the PO/contracting flow and can confirm invoice cadence and payment terms. If you prefer Marketplace billing, that typically maps to usage-based billing via AWS and can simplify procurement approvals — we can support both.

(Quoted)
> - Marketplace: Yes — if you can be listed on AWS Marketplace and support consolidated billing, that speeds procurement and our security review.

Marketplace note:
- We are available on AWS Marketplace (listing is live) and can enable consolidated billing and metered usage. Listing helps with procurement approvals and often speeds PO issuance.

(Quoted)
> - Deployment: For general user-facing product we prefer hosted. For PII-sensitive models certain teams will require either Dedicated reserved pools or Private (VPC) depending on data residency.

Packaging summary (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API): lowest friction, card or invoiced billing; on-demand pricing or commit bands (1/6/12 months) that reduce unit cost.
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): monthly/annual commits for guaranteed GPU pools; recommended for sustained PII workloads that need predictable throughput.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for regulated or air-gapped workloads; enterprise contract + onboarding lead time.

Pricing & commits (example ranges, ballspark):
- Hosted on-demand: $X per 1K tokens (baseline)
- Hosted 12mo commit: ~30% discount vs on-demand (depends on commit size)
- Dedicated: reserved monthly capacity; pricing depends on GPU type and sustained throughput — Aditya will provide a couple sizing scenarios.

Next steps:
1) Aditya — can you confirm recommended commit bands and provide a pricing summary worksheet for a 12mo commit vs on-demand? (I’ve attached pricing_summary.xlsx placeholder)
2) Alex / procurement — please send the completed procurement questionnaire or any standard PO terms.
3) If marketplace routing is preferred, Soojin will surface the AWS Marketplace ordering guide and timing to get your procurement team setup.

I’ll follow up with a concise commercial note + ranges later today so you can take to finance. Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
